title: Rensselaer County official locality target universe
summary: Official Rensselaer County and New York State property-tax records establish a 22-jurisdiction Rensselaer County city/town/village target universe: 2 cities, 14 towns, and 6 villages. This is a deterministic jurisdiction baseline for later locality-to-operator recursion and does not assert that every locality has a police agency, ALPR deployment, Flock contract, shared network, or reader.

sources.title: Participating Jurisdictions
sources.notes: Official county page states every city, town, and village in Rensselaer County formally participates and enumerates the municipality names used to bound this inventory.

sources.title: Delinquent Property Tax Information — Town SWIS codes
sources.notes: Current county guidance lists the SWIS rows used on its tax site, including city/town rows, village rows, town-outside-village rows, and split-village rows; it also states hamlets have no official status and no SWIS codes.

sources.title: SWIS Codes — Municipal Reference List
sources.publisher: New York State Office of Real Property Tax Services
sources.notes: Official ORPTS Municipal Reference List cross-checks Rensselaer city/town/village SWIS identities.

sources.title: Tax base growth factors for cities and towns — 2026
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
sources.notes: Current state table cross-checks the two cities and fourteen towns in Rensselaer County.

sources.title: RPTL Section 1402 — Village assessment options
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
sources.notes: State village-status records cross-check Nassau, East Nassau, Hoosick Falls and split-village SWIS handling relevant to the county village universe.

counterevidence: None of the municipal/tax sources establishes police-department existence, law-enforcement service boundaries, ALPR deployment, Flock vendor identity, reader ownership, platform administration, sharing state, or query activity for a listed locality.
gaps: Each municipality still requires separate public-safety/operator enumeration before any vendor/reader recursion.
County-level entities, campuses, special districts, private operators, and other non-municipal surfaces remain outside this municipality baseline.
Native Flock Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, users/admins, configuration, approval/effective-date, and query/event evidence remain unresolved for #1894.
caveats: SWIS contains town-outside-village and split-village rows used for assessment; municipality counting must not double-count a village once per containing town.
Village of Nassau spans Nassau and Schodack tax rows; Valley Falls spans Pittstown and Schaghticoke rows. Each is counted once as a municipality.
The county explicitly notes hamlets have no official municipal status/SWIS identity, so hamlets are not added to the municipality count.

data.question: What is the official city/town/village jurisdiction universe that request #1894 should recurse across before enumerating operators, vendors, readers, owners, and administrators?
data.method: Cross-checked Rensselaer County's official municipality enumeration and current county SWIS guidance against New York State ORPTS/Tax records; deduplicated split-village/town-specific rows to distinct municipal identities.
data.framework: Jurisdiction existence is a weaker evidence layer than operator existence, deployment, vendor contract, reader inventory, sharing configuration, administration, or platform use; each later layer requires separate evidence.
data.scope: Public government jurisdiction metadata only; no private-person enrichment and no inference of law-enforcement technology use.
findings: City/town universe (16): 381400 City of Rensselaer; 381700 City of Troy; 382000 Town of Berlin; 382200 Town of Brunswick; 382400 Town of East Greenbush; 382600 Town of Grafton; 382800 Town of Hoosick; 383000 Town of Nassau; 383200 Town of North Greenbush; 383400 Town of Petersburgh; 383600 Town of Pittstown; 383800 Town of Poestenkill; 384000 Town of Sand Lake; 384200 Town of Schaghticoke; 384400 Town of Schodack; 384600 Town of Stephentown.
Village universe (6 distinct identities): 384401 Castleton-on-Hudson; 383003 East Nassau; 382801 Hoosick Falls; 383001 Nassau; 384201 Schaghticoke; 383601 Valley Falls.

The county tax surface also carries town-specific/split rows including 384403 Nassau under Schodack and 384203 Valley Falls under Schaghticoke, plus town-outside-village rows such as 382889/383089/383689/384289/384489. These assessment rows are not additional municipalities.

The resulting deterministic municipality target universe contains 22 distinct city/town/village jurisdictions before separate enumeration of police departments, sheriff/county entities, campuses, special districts, private operators, or other public-safety operators.
Rensselaer County explicitly states hamlets have no official municipal status and no SWIS codes; they therefore are not municipality targets in this baseline.
conclusions: Request #1894 now has a source-backed bounded municipality universe for systematic locality recursion rather than ad hoc town selection.

The locality baseline must not be upgraded into claims about police agencies, ALPR deployments, Flock contracts, reader ownership, platform administrators, sharing relationships, or platform activity without separate source evidence.
recommendations: Enumerate public-safety operators for each of the 22 municipalities, preserving municipalities with no separate police agency as negative/coverage results rather than inventing an operator.
For each resolved operator, recurse separately into vendor, contract, reader inventory, ownership, administrator, native sharing/audit, and query/event evidence.
Enumerate non-municipal Rensselaer operators in a separate bounded pass so this municipality baseline remains semantically clean.
counterarguments: SWIS is a property-tax jurisdiction system, not a law-enforcement roster; using it directly as a police-agency list would overstate what the source proves.
limitations: The ORPTS Municipal Reference List is an older reference publication, so the county's current official municipality/SWIS pages and the 2026 state city/town table were used as current cross-checks.
No actor/operator lookup was executed for the 22 localities in this bounded pass.
unresolved: Which of the 22 municipalities operate their own police/public-safety agency versus receive service from another operator?
Which resolved operators currently or historically used Flock, Axon, or another ALPR vendor?
What non-municipal Rensselaer operators must be added to the county-wide target universe?
